avoid: low-contrast gray-on-gray muted tiers (H-23: rebalance one shade darker)
strategy: One current step foregrounded at a time; everything else recedes
Phase/step rail uses compact rows with status marks, not cards
Instructions as short imperative lines; each gate is its own bounded block
Irreversible steps get a red-flag band plus dedicated recovery block — emphasis via color+icon+position, not extra density
Generous whitespace around the work region; no persistent chrome beyond the three regions

primary: Current step: instruction, its gates (checklist / value check / confirmation), and its action
Position and progress: which phase, which step, how far to go (always visible)
Irreversible-step status: confirmation requirement and recovery path, visible before and after execution
secondary: Audit trail of gates passed, confirmations, verifications, contingencies
Runbook metadata (title, change ref, abort rule)

avoid: low-contrast gray-on-gray muted tiers (H-23: rebalance one shade darker)
strategy: One current step foregrounded at a time; everything else recedes
Phase/step rail uses compact rows with status marks, not cards
Instructions as short imperative lines; each gate is its own bounded block
Irreversible steps get a red-flag band plus dedicated recovery block — emphasis via color+icon+position, not extra density
Generous whitespace around the work region; no persistent chrome beyond the three regions

primary: Current step: instruction, its gates (checklist / value check / confirmation), and its action
Position and progress: which phase, which step, how far to go (always visible)
Irreversible-step status: confirmation requirement and recovery path, visible before and after execution
secondary: Audit trail of gates passed, confirmations, verifications, contingencies
Runbook metadata (title, change ref, abort rule)
Contingency branch outcomes

major_choices.choice: Irreversible steps gate on a typed-phrase confirmation modal naming the exact action; the primary button stays disabled until the phrase matches
major_choices.rationale: Acceptance seed demands a confirmation path; typed-phrase beats a bare OK for high-consequence actions (P-28 tradeoff: friction is intentional here)

major_choices.choice: Steps whose real-world effect has an undo window expose Rollback inline after execution, with the window length shown; steps without one show their documented recovery procedure persistently
major_choices.rationale: Covers both recovery classes: in-app undo and documented out-of-band recovery

major_choices.choice: Audit trail is a permanent third region, appended on every gate pass/confirm/recover/contingency event
major_choices.rationale: Zero-mistake completion must be provable; P-26 status visibility

major_choices.choice: Progression is hard-blocked: a step cannot be completed until every gate passes; future steps are visible but locked
major_choices.rationale: Makes 'zero mistakes' the path of least resistance rather than an aspiration

major_choices.choice: Concrete scenario: a production release runbook (pre-flight, backup, cutover, verify, finalize) with 3 irreversible steps — read-only mode flip, database migration, old-version cleanup
major_choices.rationale: Brief fixes shape, not content; a release runbook naturally exhibits high hierarchy, medium volatility (runtime values to verify) and medium uncertainty (contingency branches)

rationale: Router-returned pattern PAT-APPLICATION-SHELL (Application Shell), inspected at L2

Shell specialization: stable regions (1) phase/step rail (hierarchical tree with status), (2) gated step work region (one current step, foregrounded, blocking until gates pass), (3) audit/recovery column (event trail + recovery paths for executed irreversible steps)
Single workflow, high hierarchy → a persistent phase/step rail makes position and progress visible without navigation (P-03, P-26)
Zero-mistake success → the work region foregrounds exactly one step and hard-blocks completion until its gates pass; structure enforces correctness instead of attention (P-28)
Acceptance seed (irreversible steps have recovery/confirmation paths) → confirm-then-act modal before, recovery path + undo window after, always visible (P-28)
Low density → spacious single-focus work region; shell chrome stays minimal to avoid over-navigation (PAT-APPLICATION-SHELL tradeoff)
Medium volatility/uncertainty → value-check gates verify observed runtime values; failed checks branch to documented contingencies instead of dead ends

representation.justification_vs_shape: One workflow with high hierarchy and linear execution maps to a wizard's gated linear progression; the tree rail adds the hierarchy/position layer wizards usually lack; the form representation covers per-gate input; the feed covers the audit trail; no shape facet (comparison none, spatiality none, temporality low) motivates table/grid/map/chart

primary.reason: Consequential flow = linear gated progression with forward/back control; wizard is the canonical representation for one hierarchical procedure executed step-by-step (brief verb: complete)

rejected.reason: Prose hides gates inside text; cannot block progression or prove zero-mistake completion
Flat list loses the required high hierarchy (phases) and cannot host per-step confirmation/recovery affordances
Comparison need is none; a table would inflate density against the low-density shape
No spatial facet (spatiality none); excluded by routing on task scope and density scope

supporting.reason: Phase/step rail exposes the high hierarchy and current position persistently
Each gate (checklist items, observed-value inputs, typed confirmation) is a bounded form unit
Audit trail is an append-only event feed

rejected.reason: Loses foregrounding of the current step; irreversible confirmations would drift out of view
Breaks the one-main-screen constraint and the persistent audit/rail regions

rejected.option: Optimistic UI with post-hoc undo only
rejected.reason: Insufficient for irreversible steps; confirmation must precede the action, not follow it

Design the app: "Runway — Release Runbook Runner" (name it something like "Gatekeeper"? Keep sober: "Runbook: Release v2.4.0 → production").

Content — release runbook with 5 phases, ~12 steps:

Phase 1 Pre-flight (3 steps):
1. Verify CI status on release commit — value check: enter CI run id? Gate: checklist (green CI on HEAD, no open SEV incidents) + value check: commit SHA matches expected (short SHA "9f3ce21").
2. Confirm deploy window & comms — checklist: change ticket approved, status page notice published, #ops notified.
3. Freeze deploys — reversible action step: checklist + mark done (reversible; can unfreeze).

Phase 2 Safeguard (2 steps):
4. Take pre-deploy backup — checklist: snapshot completed; value check: backup id format (e.g., "bk-2026-10-25-0930" entered matches expected pattern? Better: enter backup id, any non-empty matches "recorded"? To keep zero-mistake semantics deterministic, value checks compare to an expected literal. I'll give expected values in the data (like from monitoring).
5. Flip maintenance/read-only mode — IRREVERSIBLE? Mode flip is reversible technically. Make this one reversible-but-gated? The brief needs 3 irreversible. Let me structure:

Phase 3 Cutover (3 steps):
6. Run database migration (migrate to v74) — IRREVERSIBLE with typed confirmation "MIGRATE PRODUCTION DATABASE", undo window: none at DB level but there's documented rollback via backup restore (recovery path: restore snapshot bk-...). Undo window 0 → recovery path documented only. Hmm, MC-2 wants at least one step with undo window. 
7. Promote new release to production (traffic cutover) — IRREVERSIBLE, typed confirmation "PROMOTE BUILD 2.4.0", undo window: 15 minutes (previous version retained; Rollback available 15 min: re-point traffic to 2.3.9). In-app rollback returns step to not-executed and logs event, app goes back to this step awaiting re-execution? Realistic: after rollback of cutover, the runbook step state becomes "recovered" and flow can proceed down contingency or re-execute. Simulating: rollback reverts step to pending (current pointer moves back), audit logs "rolled back".
8. Verify production health — value checks: enter error rate observed "0.02%" (expected "< 0.1%"), p95 latency "280ms" (expected "< 400ms"), checklist: dashboards green 10 min. Contingency: if verification fails → contingency branch: roll back to 2.3.9 (which links to step 7's rollback) + abort path.

Phase 4 Finalize (2 steps):
9. Purge old build artifacts & scale down 2.3.9 — IRREVERSIBLE, typed confirmation "RETIRED 2.3.9", no undo window; recovery path: redeploy from artifact registry (documented, slower). Only enabled after step 8 passed.
10. Unfreeze deploys & close change ticket — reversible checklist step.

Phase 5 Post (1 step):
11. Publish release note & tag — checklist.

Hmm wait, maintenance mode flip (step 5) — let me make it IRREVERSIBLE? No — better to have irreversible exactly where domain-realistic: DB migration, traffic cutover, old-version retirement. 3 irreversible steps. Mode flip stays reversible w/ checklist.

Also include contingency on step 6: if migration fails → contingency: restore backup + abort (documented). And on step 8: fail → contingency branch to roll back.

Zero-mistake scoring: "mistakes" = attempts to advance with unmet gates (blocked, counted as near-miss?), failing value checks. Keep an integrity counter? The success standard "零失误走完全程" — completion certificate: when step 11 done, show completion banner "Runbook complete — 0 mistakes" with stats: confirmations performed, checks verified, events logged. Track "blocked advance attempts" as warnings. Keep it lightweight: completion panel shows summary + audit log export (copy to clipboard as text).

State machine details:
- Steps list flat ordered with phase grouping. current pointer = first non-done step (or selected step for review).
- Rail: phases as groups, steps as rows: status icon (locked 🔒, current ○, pending gates, done ✓, irreversible flag ⚠). Click behavior: completed → reopen read-only; current → focus; future locked → blocked (no-op + shake/hint).
- Work region: step number/title, kind badges (REVERSIBLE/IRREVERSIBLE), instruction lines, gates:
  - checklist gate: items with checkboxes; all must check.
  - value gate(s): fields with expected pattern; on "Verify" click compare normalized input vs expected → pass (record + lock) or fail (record failed verification as warning event + reveal contingency).
  - action: for reversible steps: button "Mark step complete" enabled when gates pass. For irreversible: button "Execute …" opens modal; modal has recovery path summary + blast radius + typed phrase; Execute disabled until phrase matches; on confirm → execute, append audit events (confirmation + execution), set undo window timer if any (15:00 countdown for cutover; others none).
  - undo window: banner in work region + audit column entry with countdown; Rollback button → reverts step to pending (and steps after it? For cutover rollback, subsequent steps 8-11 reset to locked; current pointer returns to step 7). Audit logs rollback.
  - After window expires (or no window): recovery path block shows documented manual recovery steps (static list) — present BEFORE execution too (visible pre-execution, per acceptance "before and after").
- Back button: review earlier completed steps read-only (gates shown as satisfied, no edit).
- Advance: enabled when current step done → moves pointer next; on last step → completion state.
- Header: title "Release 2.4.0 → Production", change ref CHG-2417, progress "3/11 steps · Phase 3 of 5", abort rule: "If any check fails and recovery is not confirmed within 15 min, ABORT and roll back to 2.3.9."
- Audit column: events with timestamps (session-relative, e.g., T+00:23 from load, or clock time). Use clock time HH:MM:SS. Empty state: "No events yet — gates you pass will be recorded here."

Undo window countdown only runs while window open; expiry logs event "undo window closed". Timer per second update. 

Volatility/uncertainty: value gates embody volatility (values differ per deploy — inline "expected" values simulate today's observed system state); contingency branches embody uncertainty.

Data inlined as JS const RUNBOOK = {...}. Render with small vanilla JS. No frameworks, no network. Accessibility: aria roles, focus-visible styles, AA contrast, 44px targets.

# Gatepass — Release Runbook Runner (cell-j10-s09)

A single-page web app for **completing one high-consequence workflow with zero mistakes**:
a production release runbook (5 phases, 11 steps) where progression is hard-blocked until every
gate passes, every **irreversible** step requires a typed-phrase confirmation, and every
irreversible step carries a **recovery path** (plus an in-app rollback during its undo window).

## Run

No build, no dependencies, no network. Either:

- open `index.html` directly in a browser, or
- serve statically, e.g. `python -m http.server 8377` → http://localhost:8377/

The full runbook is inlined in the page — the first screen is usable at paint (no loading state).

## Demo walkthrough values

| Step | Gate | Value to enter |
|---|---|---|
| 1 Verify release readiness | Release commit (short SHA) | `9f3ce21` |
| 4 Take pre-deploy backup | Snapshot ID | `bk-1025-0930` |
| 6 Run DB migration (irreversible) | Rows in audit_ledger | `1,048,320` · confirm phrase `MIGRATE DB-PROD-1` |
| 7 Promote build 2.4.0 (irreversible) | Canary error rate | `0.02%` · confirm phrase `PROMOTE 2.4.0` · 15:00 undo window |
| 8 Verify production health | Error rate / p95 latency | `0.03%` / `287` (enter a wrong value first to see the contingency) |
| 9 Retire build 2.3.9 (irreversible) | — | confirm phrase `RETIRED 2.3.9` |

Checklist gates: tick every item. Value gates: type the observed value and press **Verify**.
A failed verification opens the step's **contingency** and is recorded as a warning in the audit trail.

## Design contract (Prax session ds_20261025133733_6fd6a634)

- Pattern: PAT-APPLICATION-SHELL — rail (phase/step tree) · gated work region · audit/recovery column
- Representation: wizard (gated linear progression) + tree / form / feed as supporting
- Acceptance: irreversible ⇒ typed confirmation before, recovery path before & after;
  progression blocked until gates pass; mismatches route to contingency; audit records every event

## Keyboard

Tab / Shift+Tab through rail, checkboxes, value inputs, Verify, and action buttons; focus rings visible.
Modal: Esc or **Cancel (safe)** closes; **Confirm & execute** enables only on exact phrase match.

Base directory for this skill: C:\Users\SiChuchen\.claude\plugins\cache\superpowers-marketplace\superpowers-chrome\3.0.1\skills\browsing

# Browsing with Chrome Direct

## Overview

Control Chrome via DevTools Protocol using the `use_browser` MCP tool. Single unified interface with auto-starting Chrome.

**Announce:** "I'm using the browsing skill to control Chrome."

## When to Use

**Use this when:**
- Controlling authenticated sessions
- Managing multiple tabs in running browser
- Playwright MCP unavailable or excessive

**Use Playwright MCP when:**
- Need fresh browser instances
- Generating screenshots/PDFs
- Prefer higher-level abstractions

## Auto-Capture

Every DOM action (navigate, click, type, select, eval, keyboard_press, hover, drag_drop, double_click, right_click, file_upload) automatically saves:
- `{prefix}.png` — viewport screenshot
- `{prefix}.md` — page content as structured markdown
- `{prefix}.html` — full rendered DOM
- `{prefix}-console.txt` — browser console messages

Files are saved to the session directory with sequential prefixes (001-navigate, 002-click, etc.). You must check these before using extract or screenshot actions.

## The use_browser Tool

Single MCP tool with action-based interface. Chrome auto-starts on first use.

**Parameters:**
- `action` (required): Operation to perform
- `selector` (optional): CSS or XPath selector for element operations
- `payload` (optional): Action-specific data (string or object)
- `timeout` (optional): Timeout in ms for await operations (default: 5000)

**Active tab**: Every action operates on the current `activeTab`. Use `switch_tab` to change it.

## Actions Reference

### Navigation
- **navigate**: Navigate to URL
  - `payload`: URL string
  - Example: `{action: "navigate", payload: "https://example.com"}`

- **await_element**: Wait for element to appear
  - `selector`: CSS selector
  - `timeout`: Max wait time in ms
  - Example: `{action: "await_element", selector: ".loaded", timeout: 10000}`

- **await_text**: Wait for text to appear
  - `payload`: Text to wait for
  - Example: `{action: "await_text", payload: "Welcome"}`

### Interaction
- **click**: Click element
  - `selector`: CSS selector
  - Example: `{action: "click", selector: "button.submit"}`

- **type**: Text input
  - `selector`: Optional — clicks to focus first
  - `payload`: Text to type (`\t`=Tab, `\n`=Enter)
  - Example: `{action: "type", selector: "#email", payload: "user@example.com"}`

- **double_click**: Double-click element (fires dblclick event)
  - `selector`: CSS selector
  - Example: `{action: "double_click", selector: ".item"}`

- **right_click**: Right-click element (fires contextmenu event)
  - `selector`: CSS selector
  - Example: `{action: "right_click", selector: ".row"}`

- **select**: Select dropdown option
  - `selector`: CSS selector
  - `payload`: Option value(s)
  - Example: `{action: "select", selector: "select[name=state]", payload: "CA"}`

- **keyboard_press**: Press special keys (Tab, Enter, Escape, Arrow keys, F1-F12)
  - `payload`: Key name (string) or `{"key": "Tab", "modifiers": {"shift": true, "ctrl": false, "alt": false, "meta": false}}`
  - Example: `{action: "keyboard_press", payload: "Tab"}`
  - Example with modifiers: `{action: "keyboard_press", payload: {"key": "Tab", "modifiers": {"shift": true}}}`

### Mouse Actions (CDP-Level)
These use CDP Input.dispatchMouseEvent, bypassing synthetic event restrictions.

- **hover**: Move mouse over element (CSS :hover, tooltips, menus)
  - `selector`: CSS selector
  - Example: `{action: "hover", selector: ".menu-trigger"}`

- **drag_drop**: Drag element to target (native drag-and-drop via CDP)
  - `selector`: Source element
  - `payload`: Target selector or JSON coordinates `{"x":N,"y":N}`
  - Example: `{action: "drag_drop", selector: ".card", payload: ".column-2"}`

- **mouse_move**: Move mouse to coordinates
  - `payload`: JSON `{"x":N,"y":N}` (optional: `steps`, `fromX`, `fromY` for smooth movement)
  - Example: `{action: "mouse_move", payload: "{\"x\":100,\"y\":200}"}`

- **scroll**: Scroll via mouse wheel events
  - `payload`: Direction (up/down/left/right) or JSON `{"deltaX":N,"deltaY":N}`
  - `selector`: Optional — scroll within element
  - Example: `{action: "scroll", payload: "down"}`

### File Upload
- **file_upload**: Set files on input[type=file] elements (can't be done via JavaScript)
  - `selector`: File input element
  - `payload`: File path or JSON `{"files":["/path/a.pdf","/path/b.jpg"]}`
  - Example: `{action: "file_upload", selector: "#upload", payload: "/tmp/doc.pdf"}`

### Extraction
- **extract**: Get page content
  - `payload`: Format ('markdown'|'text'|'html')
  - `selector`: Optional - limit to element
  - Example: `{action: "extract", payload: "markdown"}`
  - Example: `{action: "extract", payload: "text", selector: "h1"}`

- **attr**: Get element attribute
  - `selector`: CSS selector
  - `payload`: Attribute name
  - Example: `{action: "attr", selector: "a.download", payload: "href"}`

- **eval**: Execute JavaScript
  - `payload`: JavaScript code
  - Example: `{action: "eval", payload: "document.title"}`

### Export
- **screenshot**: Capture screenshot of a specific element
  - `payload`: Filename
  - `selector`: Optional - screenshot specific element
  - Viewport screenshots are auto-captured after every DOM action. Use this only when you need a specific element.
  - Example: `{action: "screenshot", payload: "/tmp/chart.png", selector: ".chart"}`

### Tab Management
- **list_tabs**: List all open tabs
  - Example: `{action: "list_tabs"}`

- **new_tab**: Create new tab
  - Example: `{action: "new_tab"}`

- **close_tab**: Close the active tab
  - Example: `{action: "close_tab"}`

- **switch_tab**: Switch the active tab (sticky — stays until changed)
  - `payload`: Tab index (number), URL substring, or title substring
  - Example: `{action: "switch_tab", payload: 1}` (by index)
  - Example: `{action: "switch_tab", payload: "example.com"}` (by URL substring)
  - Example: `{action: "switch_tab", payload: "GitHub"}` (by title substring)

### Browser Mode Control
- **show_browser**: Make browser window visible (headed mode)
  - Example: `{action: "show_browser"}`
  - ⚠️ **WARNING**: Restarts Chrome, reloads pages via GET, loses POST state

- **hide_browser**: Switch to headless mode (invisible browser)
  - Example: `{action: "hide_browser"}`
  - ⚠️ **WARNING**: Restarts Chrome, reloads pages via GET, loses POST state

- **browser_mode**: Check current browser mode, port, and profile
  - Example: `{action: "browser_mode"}`
  - Returns: `{"headless": true|false, "mode": "headless"|"headed", "running": true|false, "port": 9222, "profile": "name", "profileDir": "/path"}`

### Profile Management
- **set_profile**: Change Chrome profile (must kill Chrome first)
  - Example: `{action: "set_profile", "payload": "browser-user"}`
  - ⚠️ **WARNING**: Chrome must be stopped first
  - **Side effect**: marks the profile as explicit, opting out of auto-disambiguation (see below)

- **get_profile**: Get current profile name and directory
  - Example: `{action: "get_profile"}`
  - Returns: `{"profile": "name", "profileDir": "/path"}`

**Default behavior**: Chrome starts in **headless mode** with **"superpowers-chrome" profile** on a **dynamically allocated port** (range 9222-12111). Override the port with `CHROME_WS_PORT`; override the profile with `CHROME_WS_PROFILE`.

**Auto-disambiguation across parallel MCPs**:
When two MCP servers start on the same host with the default profile, the first claims `superpowers-chrome` (port 9222) and later ones silently fall through to `superpowers-chrome-2` (port 9223), `superpowers-chrome-3`, etc. Each MCP drives its own Chrome with its own profile dir; they don't fight over `activeTab`. The bridge tracks ownership via a lock file at `~/.cache/superpowers/browser-profiles/<profile>.mcp.lock`; stale locks (dead PIDs) are reclaimed automatically.

To opt **out** of disambiguation — e.g., to intentionally share Chrome between a long-lived `chrome-ws` CLI session and your MCP — set the profile name explicitly:
- Env var: `CHROME_WS_PROFILE=my-profile`
- Or: `{action: "set_profile", payload: "my-profile"}` at runtime

An explicit profile name still acquires the lock, but on conflict the bridge **shares** rather than disambiguates — the second process reconnects to the first's Chrome (the original reconnect-on-restart behavior).

### Chrome Lifecycle (Recovery)
- **kill_chrome**: Kill the Chrome process this MCP is driving
  - Example: `{action: "kill_chrome"}`
  - Releases the meta.json; next page action auto-restarts Chrome

- **restart_chrome**: kill_chrome + immediate spawn
  - Example: `{action: "restart_chrome"}`

**Auto-restart banner**: when the bridge has to spawn a fresh Chrome (because the previous one died or was killed externally — e.g., `kill -9 <pid>` from the shell), the first response after the restart prepends:
```
[Chrome auto-restarted; URL reset to about:blank. Re-navigate to continue.]
```
Treat this as a signal that your prior URL / tab state is gone — re-navigate before assuming anything about the current page.

### Console Logging
Capture browser console output for the active tab. Buffer is keyed by the page session's `sessionId`, so it survives `close_tab`/`new_tab` ordering quirks. Levels: `log`, `info`, `warn`, `error`.

- **enable_console_logging**: Start capturing
  - Example: `{action: "enable_console_logging"}`

- **get_console_messages**: Read captured messages
  - All: `{action: "get_console_messages"}`
  - Since timestamp (epoch ms): `{action: "get_console_messages", payload: {since: 1716000000000}}`
  - Returns: array of `{timestamp, level, text}` entries

- **clear_console_messages**: Reset the buffer
  - Example: `{action: "clear_console_messages"}`

### Dialog Handling
Native dialogs (JS alert/confirm/prompt, beforeunload, HTTP basic-auth, permission prompts, device choosers) pause the page. While a dialog is open, page-targeted actions (`extract`, `click`, `eval`, etc.) return a refusal whose text contains `Page is behind a dialog` and lists the available `dialog::*` selectors.

When a dialog fires **during** a `navigate` (typical for HTTP basic-auth), `navigate` itself throws with the dialog grammar in the message — you don't have to issue a separate page-targeted call to discover the dialog.

Handle dialogs by clicking/typing a `dialog::*` selector:
- `{action: "click", selector: "dialog::accept"}` — accept JS alert/confirm/prompt, beforeunload, permission grant
- `{action: "click", selector: "dialog::dismiss"}` — dismiss / cancel / deny
- `{action: "type", selector: "dialog::prompt", payload: "text"}` then accept — respond to JS prompt
- `{action: "type", selector: "dialog::username", payload: "alice"}` + `{action: "type", selector: "dialog::password", payload: "secret"}` + `{action: "click", selector: "dialog::accept"}` — HTTP basic-auth
- `{action: "click", selector: "dialog::device[id=\"<deviceId>\"]"}` — pick a WebUSB/Bluetooth/Serial/HID device

**Critical caveats when toggling modes**:
1. **Chrome must restart** - Cannot switch headless/headed mode on running Chrome
2. **Pages reload via GET** - All open tabs are reopened with GET requests
3. **POST state is lost** - Form submissions, POST results, and POST-based navigation will be lost
4. **Session state is lost** - Any client-side state (JavaScript variables, etc.) is cleared
5. **Cookies/auth may persist** - Uses same user data directory, so logged-in sessions may survive

**When to use headed mode**:

- Demonstrating browser behavior to user

# Browsing with Chrome Direct

## Overview

Control Chrome via DevTools Protocol using the `use_browser` MCP tool. Single unified interface with auto-starting Chrome.

**Announce:** "I'm using the browsing skill to control Chrome."

## When to Use

**Use this when:**
- Controlling authenticated sessions
- Managing multiple tabs in running browser
- Playwright MCP unavailable or excessive

**Use Playwright MCP when:**
- Need fresh browser instances
- Generating screenshots/PDFs
- Prefer higher-level abstractions

## Auto-Capture

Every DOM action (navigate, click, type, select, eval, keyboard_press, hover, drag_drop, double_click, right_click, file_upload) automatically saves:
- `{prefix}.png` — viewport screenshot
- `{prefix}.md` — page content as structured markdown
- `{prefix}.html` — full rendered DOM
- `{prefix}-console.txt` — browser console messages

Files are saved to the session directory with sequential prefixes (001-navigate, 002-click, etc.). You must check these before using extract or screenshot actions.

## The use_browser Tool

Single MCP tool with action-based interface. Chrome auto-starts on first use.

**Parameters:**
- `action` (required): Operation to perform
- `selector` (optional): CSS or XPath selector for element operations
- `payload` (optional): Action-specific data (string or object)
- `timeout` (optional): Timeout in ms for await operations (default: 5000)

**Active tab**: Every action operates on the current `activeTab`. Use `switch_tab` to change it.

- **navigate**: Navigate to URL
  - `payload`: URL string
  - Example: `{action: "navigate", payload: "https://example.com"}`

- **await_element**: Wait for element to appear
  - `selector`: CSS selector
  - `timeout`: Max wait time in ms
  - Example: `{action: "await_element", selector: ".loaded", timeout: 10000}`

- **await_text**: Wait for text to appear
  - `payload`: Text to wait for
  - Example: `{action: "await_text", payload: "Welcome"}`

### Interaction
- **click**: Click element
  - `selector`: CSS selector
  - Example: `{action: "click", selector: "button.submit"}`

- **type**: Text input
  - `selector`: Optional — clicks to focus first
  - `payload`: Text to type (`\t`=Tab, `\n`=Enter)
  - Example: `{action: "type", selector: "#email", payload: "user@example.com"}`

- **double_click**: Double-click element (fires dblclick event)
  - `selector`: CSS selector
  - Example: `{action: "double_click", selector: ".item"}`

- **right_click**: Right-click element (fires contextmenu event)
  - `selector`: CSS selector
  - Example: `{action: "right_click", selector: ".row"}`

- **select**: Select dropdown option
  - `selector`: CSS selector
  - `payload`: Option value(s)
  - Example: `{action: "select", selector: "select[name=state]", payload: "CA"}`

- **keyboard_press**: Press special keys (Tab, Enter, Escape, Arrow keys, F1-F12)
  - `payload`: Key name (string) or `{"key": "Tab", "modifiers": {"shift": true, "ctrl": false, "alt": false, "meta": false}}`
  - Example: `{action: "keyboard_press", payload: "Tab"}`
  - Example with modifiers: `{action: "keyboard_press", payload: {"key": "Tab", "modifiers": {"shift": true}}}`

### Mouse Actions (CDP-Level)
These use CDP Input.dispatchMouseEvent, bypassing synthetic event restrictions.

- **hover**: Move mouse over element (CSS :hover, tooltips, menus)
  - `selector`: CSS selector
  - Example: `{action: "hover", selector: ".menu-trigger"}`

- **drag_drop**: Drag element to target (native drag-and-drop via CDP)
  - `selector`: Source element
  - `payload`: Target selector or JSON coordinates `{"x":N,"y":N}`
  - Example: `{action: "drag_drop", selector: ".card", payload: ".column-2"}`

- **mouse_move**: Move mouse to coordinates
  - `payload`: JSON `{"x":N,"y":N}` (optional: `steps`, `fromX`, `fromY` for smooth movement)
  - Example: `{action: "mouse_move", payload: "{\"x\":100,\"y\":200}"}`

- **scroll**: Scroll via mouse wheel events
  - `payload`: Direction (up/down/left/right) or JSON `{"deltaX":N,"deltaY":N}`
  - `selector`: Optional — scroll within element
  - Example: `{action: "scroll", payload: "down"}`

### File Upload
- **file_upload**: Set files on input[type=file] elements (can't be done via JavaScript)
  - `selector`: File input element
  - `payload`: File path or JSON `{"files":["/path/a.pdf","/path/b.jpg"]}`
  - Example: `{action: "file_upload", selector: "#upload", payload: "/tmp/doc.pdf"}`

### Extraction
- **extract**: Get page content
  - `payload`: Format ('markdown'|'text'|'html')
  - `selector`: Optional - limit to element
  - Example: `{action: "extract", payload: "markdown"}`
  - Example: `{action: "extract", payload: "text", selector: "h1"}`

- **attr**: Get element attribute
  - `selector`: CSS selector
  - `payload`: Attribute name
  - Example: `{action: "attr", selector: "a.download", payload: "href"}`

- **eval**: Execute JavaScript
  - `payload`: JavaScript code
  - Example: `{action: "eval", payload: "document.title"}`

  - `payload`: Filename
  - `selector`: Optional - screenshot specific element

- **list_tabs**: List all open tabs
  - Example: `{action: "list_tabs"}`

- **new_tab**: Create new tab
  - Example: `{action: "new_tab"}`

- **close_tab**: Close the active tab
  - Example: `{action: "close_tab"}`

  - `payload`: Tab index (number), URL substring, or title substring
  - Example: `{action: "switch_tab", payload: 1}` (by index)
  - Example: `{action: "switch_tab", payload: "example.com"}` (by URL substring)

- **show_browser**: Make browser window visible (headed mode)
  - Example: `{action: "show_browser"}`
  - ⚠️ **WARNING**: Restarts Chrome, reloads pages via GET, loses POST state

  - Example: `{action: "hide_browser"}`
  - ⚠️ **WARNING**: Restarts Chrome, reloads pages via GET, loses POST state

  - Returns: `{"headless": true|false, "mode": "headless"|"headed", "running": true|false, "port": 9222, "profile": "name", "profileDir": "/path"}`

When two MCP servers start on the same host with the default profile, the first claims `superpowers-chrome` (port 9222) and later ones silently fall through to `superpowers-chrome-2` (port 9223), `superpowers-chrome-3`, etc. Each MCP drives its own Chrome with its own profile dir; they don't fight over `activeTab`. **Auto-disambiguation across parallel MCPs**:
When two MCP servers start on the same host with the default profile, the first claims `superpowers-chrome` (port 9222) and later ones silently fall through to `superpowers-chrome-2` (port 9223), `superpowers-chrome-3`, etc. Each MCP drives its own Chrome with its own profile dir; they don't fight over `activeTab`. - Or: `{action: "set_profile", payload: "my-profile"}` at runtime


- Demonstrating browser behavior to user
- Testing features that only work with visible browser
- Debugging issues that don't reproduce in headless mode

- Most automation works identically in both modes

  - Example: browser-user agent uses "browser-user" profile
- **Task-specific profiles**: Testing with different user contexts
  - Example: "test-logged-in" vs "test-logged-out"

- Chrome restarts
- Mode toggles (headless ↔ headed)
- System reboots (data is in cache directory)

```
{action: "extract", payload: "text", selector: "h1"}

```

```
{action: "await_text", payload: "Welcome"}
```

Uses `keyboard_press` to submit the form.

```

{action: "switch_tab", payload: 2}
{action: "click", selector: "a.email"}
{action: "await_element", selector: ".content"}
{action: "extract", payload: "text", selector: ".amount"}
```

```

{action: "type", selector: "input[name=q]", payload: "query"}
{action: "click", selector: "button.search"}
{action: "await_element", selector: ".results"}
{action: "extract", payload: "text", selector: ".result-title"}
```

  - Example: `{action: "restart_chrome"}`

**Auto-restart banner**: when the bridge has to spawn a fresh Chrome (because the previous one died or was killed externally — e.g., `kill -9 <pid>` from the shell), the first response after the restart prepends:
```
[Chrome auto-restarted; URL reset to about:blank. Re-navigate to continue.]
```
Treat this as a signal that your prior URL / tab state is gone — re-navigate before assuming anything about the current page.

### Console Logging
Capture browser console output for the active tab. Buffer is keyed by the page session's `sessionId`, so it survives `close_tab`/`new_tab` ordering quirks. Levels: `log`, `info`, `warn`, `error`.

- **enable_console_logging**: Start capturing
  - Example: `{action: "enable_console_logging"}`

- **get_console_messages**: Read captured messages
  - All: `{action: "get_console_messages"}`
  - Since timestamp (epoch ms): `{action: "get_console_messages", payload: {since: 1716000000000}}`
  - Returns: array of `{timestamp, level, text}` entries

- **clear_console_messages**: Reset the buffer
  - Example: `{action: "clear_console_messages"}`

### Dialog Handling
Native dialogs (JS alert/confirm/prompt, beforeunload, HTTP basic-auth, permission prompts, device choosers) pause the page. While a dialog is open, page-targeted actions (`extract`, `click`, `eval`, etc.) return a refusal whose text contains `Page is behind a dialog` and lists the available `dialog::*` selectors.

When a dialog fires **during** a `navigate` (typical for HTTP basic-auth), `navigate` itself throws with the dialog grammar in the message — you don't have to issue a separate page-targeted call to discover the dialog.

Handle dialogs by clicking/typing a `dialog::*` selector:
- `{action: "click", selector: "dialog::accept"}` — accept JS alert/confirm/prompt, beforeunload, permission grant
- `{action: "click", selector: "dialog::dismiss"}` — dismiss / cancel / deny
- `{action: "type", selector: "dialog::prompt", payload: "text"}` then accept — respond to JS prompt
- `{action: "type", selector: "dialog::username", payload: "alice"}` + `{action: "type", selector: "dialog::password", payload: "secret"}` + `{action: "click", selector: "dialog::accept"}` — HTTP basic-auth
- `{action: "click", selector: "dialog::device[id=\"<deviceId>\"]"}` — pick a WebUSB/Bluetooth/Serial/HID device

**Critical caveats when toggling modes**:
1. **Chrome must restart** - Cannot switch headless/headed mode on running Chrome
2. **Pages reload via GET** - All open tabs are reopened with GET requests
3. **POST state is lost** - Form submissions, POST results, and POST-based navigation will be lost
4. **Session state is lost** - Any client-side state (JavaScript variables, etc.) is cleared
5. **Cookies/auth may persist** - Uses same user data directory, so logged-in sessions may survive

**When to use headed mode**:
- Debugging visual rendering issues
- Demonstrating browser behavior to user
- Testing features that only work with visible browser
- Debugging issues that don't reproduce in headless mode

**When to stay in headless mode** (default):
- All other cases - faster, cleaner, less intrusive
- Screenshots work perfectly in headless mode
- Most automation works identically in both modes

**Profile management**:
Profiles store persistent browser data (cookies, localStorage, extensions, auth sessions).

**Profile locations**:
- macOS: `~/Library/Caches/superpowers/browser-profiles/{name}/`
- Linux: `~/.cache/superpowers/browser-profiles/{name}/`
- Windows: `%LOCALAPPDATA%/superpowers/browser-profiles/{name}/`

**When to use separate profiles**:
- **Default profile ("superpowers-chrome")**: General automation, shared sessions
- **Agent-specific profiles**: Isolate different agents' browser state
  - Example: browser-user agent uses "browser-user" profile
- **Task-specific profiles**: Testing with different user contexts
  - Example: "test-logged-in" vs "test-logged-out"

**Profile data persists across**:
- Chrome restarts
- Mode toggles (headless ↔ headed)
- System reboots (data is in cache directory)

**To use a different profile**:
1. Kill Chrome if running: `await chromeLib.killChrome()`
2. Set profile: `{action: "set_profile", "payload": "my-profile"}`
3. Start Chrome: Next navigate/action will use new profile

## Quick Start Pattern

```
Navigate and extract:
{action: "navigate", payload: "https://example.com"}
{action: "await_element", selector: "h1"}
{action: "extract", payload: "text", selector: "h1"}
```

## Common Patterns

### Fill and Submit Form
```
{action: "navigate", payload: "https://example.com/login"}
{action: "await_element", selector: "input[name=email]"}
{action: "type", selector: "input[name=email]", payload: "user@example.com"}
{action: "type", selector: "input[name=password]", payload: "pass123"}
{action: "keyboard_press", payload: "Enter"}
{action: "await_text", payload: "Welcome"}
```

Uses `keyboard_press` to submit the form.

### Multi-Tab Workflow
```
{action: "list_tabs"}
{action: "switch_tab", payload: 2}
{action: "click", selector: "a.email"}
{action: "await_element", selector: ".content"}
{action: "extract", payload: "text", selector: ".amount"}
```

### Dynamic Content
```
{action: "navigate", payload: "https://example.com"}
{action: "type", selector: "input[name=q]", payload: "query"}
{action: "click", selector: "button.search"}
{action: "await_element", selector: ".results"}
{action: "extract", payload: "text", selector: ".result-title"}
```

### Get Link Attribute
```
{action: "navigate", payload: "https://example.com"}
{action: "await_element", selector: "a.download"}
{action: "attr", selector: "a.download", payload: "href"}
```

### Execute JavaScript
```
{action: "eval", payload: "document.querySelectorAll('a').length"}
{action: "eval", payload: "Array.from(document.querySelectorAll('a')).map(a => a.href)"}
```

### Resize Viewport (Responsive Testing)
Use `eval` to resize the browser window for testing responsive layouts:
```
{action: "eval", payload: "window.resizeTo(375, 812); 'Resized to mobile'"}
{action: "eval", payload: "window.resizeTo(768, 1024); 'Resized to tablet'"}
{action: "eval", payload: "window.resizeTo(1920, 1080); 'Resized to desktop'"}
```

**Note**: This resizes the window, not device emulation. It won't change:
- Device pixel ratio (retina displays)
- Touch events
- User-Agent string

For most responsive testing, window resize is sufficient.

### Clear Cookies
Use `eval` to clear cookies accessible to JavaScript:
```
{action: "eval", payload: "document.cookie.split(';').forEach(c => { document.cookie = c.trim().split('=')[0] + '=;expires=Thu, 01 Jan 1970 00:00:00 GMT;path=/'; }); 'Cookies cleared'"}
```

**Note**: This clears cookies accessible to JavaScript. It won't clear:
- httpOnly cookies (server-side only)
- Cookies from other domains

For most logout/reset scenarios, this is sufficient.

### Scroll Page
```
{action: "scroll", payload: "down"}
{action: "scroll", payload: "up"}
{action: "scroll", selector: ".container", payload: "{\"deltaX\":0,\"deltaY\":500}"}
```

Uses real mouse wheel events (vs `eval` + `scrollTo` which bot detectors flag).

**Always wait before interaction:**
Don't click or fill immediately after navigate - pages need time to load.

```

{action: "navigate", payload: "https://example.com"}
{action: "click", selector: "button"}  // May fail!

// GOOD - wait first
{action: "navigate", payload: "https://example.com"}
{action: "await_element", selector: "button"}
{action: "click", selector: "button"}
```

**Use specific selectors:**
Avoid generic selectors that match multiple elements.

```

{action: "click", selector: "button"}

// GOOD - specific
{action: "click", selector: "button[type=submit]"}
{action: "click", selector: "#login-button"}
```

**Submit forms:**
Use `keyboard_press` with Enter after `type`, or append `\n` to the payload.

```
{action: "type", selector: "#search", payload: "query"}
{action: "keyboard_press", payload: "Enter"}
```

Extract page content to verify selectors before building workflow.

```
{action: "extract", payload: "html"}
```

**Element not found:**
- Use `await_element` before interaction
- Verify selector with `extract` action using 'html' format

**Timeout errors:**
- Increase timeout: `{timeout: 30000}` for slow pages
- Wait for specific element instead of text

**Wrong tab active:**
- Use `list_tabs` to see all open tabs
- Use `switch_tab` with a URL or title substring to reliably switch tabs
- Tab indices shift when tabs close — prefer URL/title-based switching

**eval returns `[object Object]`:**

- For async functions: `{action: "eval", payload: "JSON.stringify(await yourAsyncFunction())"}`

<summary>Click to expand test automation guidance</summary>

Best for: Single-step tests, direct Claude control during conversation

1. **Check chrome-ws source code** - It shows the correct CDP pattern
2. **Use chrome-ws to verify** - Test the same operation via CLI

### Common Test Automation Patterns
- **Form validation**: Fill forms, check error states
- **UI state testing**: Click elements, verify DOM changes
- **Performance testing**: Measure load times, capture metrics
- **Screenshot comparison**: Capture before/after states

# Browsing with Chrome Direct

## Overview

Control Chrome via DevTools Protocol using the `use_browser` MCP tool. Single unified interface with auto-starting Chrome.

**Announce:** "I'm using the browsing skill to control Chrome."

## When to Use

**Use this when:**
- Controlling authenticated sessions
- Managing multiple tabs in running browser
- Playwright MCP unavailable or excessive

**Use Playwright MCP when:**
- Need fresh browser instances
- Generating screenshots/PDFs
- Prefer higher-level abstractions

## Auto-Capture

Every DOM action (navigate, click, type, select, eval, keyboard_press, hover, drag_drop, double_click, right_click, file_upload) automatically saves:
- `{prefix}.png` — viewport screenshot
- `{prefix}.md` — page content as structured markdown
- `{prefix}.html` — full rendered DOM
- `{prefix}-console.txt` — browser console messages

Files are saved to the session directory with sequential prefixes (001-navigate, 002-click, etc.). You must check these before using extract or screenshot actions.

## The use_browser Tool

Single MCP tool with action-based interface. Chrome auto-starts on first use.

**Parameters:**
- `action` (required): Operation to perform
- `selector` (optional): CSS or XPath selector for element operations
- `payload` (optional): Action-specific data (string or object)
- `timeout` (optional): Timeout in ms for await operations (default: 5000)

**Active tab**: Every action operates on the current `activeTab`. Use `switch_tab` to change it.

## Actions Reference

### Navigation
- **navigate**: Navigate to URL
  - `payload`: URL string
  - Example: `{action: "navigate", payload: "https://example.com"}`

- **await_element**: Wait for element to appear
  - `selector`: CSS selector
  - `timeout`: Max wait time in ms
  - Example: `{action: "await_element", selector: ".loaded", timeout: 10000}`

- **await_text**: Wait for text to appear
  - `payload`: Text to wait for
  - Example: `{action: "await_text", payload: "Welcome"}`

### Interaction
- **click**: Click element
  - `selector`: CSS selector
  - Example: `{action: "click", selector: "button.submit"}`

- **type**: Text input
  - `selector`: Optional — clicks to focus first
  - `payload`: Text to type (`\t`=Tab, `\n`=Enter)
  - Example: `{action: "type", selector: "#email", payload: "user@example.com"}`

- **double_click**: Double-click element (fires dblclick event)
  - `selector`: CSS selector
  - Example: `{action: "double_click", selector: ".item"}`

- **right_click**: Right-click element (fires contextmenu event)
  - `selector`: CSS selector
  - Example: `{action: "right_click", selector: ".row"}`

- **select**: Select dropdown option
  - `selector`: CSS selector
  - `payload`: Option value(s)
  - Example: `{action: "select", selector: "select[name=state]", payload: "CA"}`

- **keyboard_press**: Press special keys (Tab, Enter, Escape, Arrow keys, F1-F12)
  - `payload`: Key name (string) or `{"key": "Tab", "modifiers": {"shift": true, "ctrl": false, "alt": false, "meta": false}}`
  - Example: `{action: "keyboard_press", payload: "Tab"}`
  - Example with modifiers: `{action: "keyboard_press", payload: {"key": "Tab", "modifiers": {"shift": true}}}`

### Mouse Actions (CDP-Level)
These use CDP Input.dispatchMouseEvent, bypassing synthetic event restrictions.

- **hover**: Move mouse over element (CSS :hover, tooltips, menus)
  - `selector`: CSS selector
  - Example: `{action: "hover", selector: ".menu-trigger"}`

- **drag_drop**: Drag element to target (native drag-and-drop via CDP)
  - `selector`: Source element
  - `payload`: Target selector or JSON coordinates `{"x":N,"y":N}`
  - Example: `{action: "drag_drop", selector: ".card", payload: ".column-2"}`

- **mouse_move**: Move mouse to coordinates
  - `payload`: JSON `{"x":N,"y":N}` (optional: `steps`, `fromX`, `fromY` for smooth movement)
  - Example: `{action: "mouse_move", payload: "{\"x\":100,\"y\":200}"}`

- **scroll**: Scroll via mouse wheel events
  - `payload`: Direction (up/down/left/right) or JSON `{"deltaX":N,"deltaY":N}`
  - `selector`: Optional — scroll within element
  - Example: `{action: "scroll", payload: "down"}`

### File Upload
- **file_upload**: Set files on input[type=file] elements (can't be done via JavaScript)
  - `selector`: File input element
  - `payload`: File path or JSON `{"files":["/path/a.pdf","/path/b.jpg"]}`
  - Example: `{action: "file_upload", selector: "#upload", payload: "/tmp/doc.pdf"}`

### Extraction
- **extract**: Get page content
  - `payload`: Format ('markdown'|'text'|'html')
  - `selector`: Optional - limit to element
  - Example: `{action: "extract", payload: "markdown"}`
  - Example: `{action: "extract", payload: "text", selector: "h1"}`

- **attr**: Get element attribute
  - `selector`: CSS selector
  - `payload`: Attribute name
  - Example: `{action: "attr", selector: "a.download", payload: "href"}`

- **eval**: Execute JavaScript
  - `payload`: JavaScript code
  - Example: `{action: "eval", payload: "document.title"}`

### Export
- **screenshot**: Capture screenshot of a specific element
  - `payload`: Filename
  - `selector`: Optional - screenshot specific element
  - Viewport screenshots are auto-captured after every DOM action. Use this only when you need a specific element.
  - Example: `{action: "screenshot", payload: "/tmp/chart.png", selector: ".chart"}`

### Tab Management
- **list_tabs**: List all open tabs
  - Example: `{action: "list_tabs"}`

- **new_tab**: Create new tab
  - Example: `{action: "new_tab"}`

- **close_tab**: Close the active tab
  - Example: `{action: "close_tab"}`

- **switch_tab**: Switch the active tab (sticky — stays until changed)
  - `payload`: Tab index (number), URL substring, or title substring
  - Example: `{action: "switch_tab", payload: 1}` (by index)
  - Example: `{action: "switch_tab", payload: "example.com"}` (by URL substring)
  - Example: `{action: "switch_tab", payload: "GitHub"}` (by title substring)

- **set_profile**: Change Chrome profile (must kill Chrome first)
  - Example: `{action: "set_profile", "payload": "browser-user"}`

  - **Side effect**: marks the profile as explicit, opting out of auto-disambiguation (see below)

- `{action: "click", selector: "dialog::accept"}` — accept JS alert/confirm/prompt, beforeunload, permission grant
- `{action: "click", selector: "dialog::dismiss"}` — dismiss / cancel / deny
- `{action: "type", selector: "dialog::prompt", payload: "text"}` then accept — respond to JS prompt
- `{action: "type", selector: "dialog::username", payload: "alice"}` + `{action: "type", selector: "dialog::password", payload: "secret"}` + `{action: "click", selector: "dialog::accept"}` — HTTP basic-auth
- `{action: "click", selector: "dialog::device[id=\"<deviceId>\"]"}` — pick a WebUSB/Bluetooth/Serial/HID device

**Critical caveats when toggling modes**:
1. **Chrome must restart** - Cannot switch headless/headed mode on running Chrome
2. **Pages reload via GET** - All open tabs are reopened with GET requests
3. **POST state is lost** - Form submissions, POST results, and POST-based navigation will be lost
4. **Session state is lost** - Any client-side state (JavaScript variables, etc.) is cleared
5. **Cookies/auth may persist** - Uses same user data directory, so logged-in sessions may survive

**When to use headed mode**:
- Debugging visual rendering issues
- Demonstrating browser behavior to user
- Testing features that only work with visible browser
- Debugging issues that don't reproduce in headless mode

**When to stay in headless mode** (default):
- All other cases - faster, cleaner, less intrusive
- Screenshots work perfectly in headless mode
- Most automation works identically in both modes

**Profile management**:
Profiles store persistent browser data (cookies, localStorage, extensions, auth sessions).

**Profile locations**:
- macOS: `~/Library/Caches/superpowers/browser-profiles/{name}/`
- Linux: `~/.cache/superpowers/browser-profiles/{name}/`
- Windows: `%LOCALAPPDATA%/superpowers/browser-profiles/{name}/`

**When to use separate profiles**:
- **Default profile ("superpowers-chrome")**: General automation, shared sessions
- **Agent-specific profiles**: Isolate different agents' browser state
  - Example: browser-user agent uses "browser-user" profile
- **Task-specific profiles**: Testing with different user contexts
  - Example: "test-logged-in" vs "test-logged-out"

**Profile data persists across**:
- Chrome restarts
- Mode toggles (headless ↔ headed)
- System reboots (data is in cache directory)

**To use a different profile**:
1. Kill Chrome if running: `await chromeLib.killChrome()`
2. Set profile: `{action: "set_profile", "payload": "my-profile"}`
3. Start Chrome: Next navigate/action will use new profile

## Quick Start Pattern

```
Navigate and extract:
{action: "navigate", payload: "https://example.com"}
{action: "await_element", selector: "h1"}
{action: "extract", payload: "text", selector: "h1"}
```

## Common Patterns

### Fill and Submit Form
```
{action: "navigate", payload: "https://example.com/login"}
{action: "await_element", selector: "input[name=email]"}
{action: "type", selector: "input[name=email]", payload: "user@example.com"}
{action: "type", selector: "input[name=password]", payload: "pass123"}
{action: "keyboard_press", payload: "Enter"}
{action: "await_text", payload: "Welcome"}
```

Uses `keyboard_press` to submit the form.

### Multi-Tab Workflow
```
{action: "list_tabs"}
{action: "switch_tab", payload: 2}
{action: "click", selector: "a.email"}
{action: "await_element", selector: ".content"}
{action: "extract", payload: "text", selector: ".amount"}
```

### Dynamic Content
```
{action: "navigate", payload: "https://example.com"}
{action: "type", selector: "input[name=q]", payload: "query"}
{action: "click", selector: "button.search"}
{action: "await_element", selector: ".results"}
{action: "extract", payload: "text", selector: ".result-title"}
```

### Get Link Attribute
```
{action: "navigate", payload: "https://example.com"}
{action: "await_element", selector: "a.download"}
{action: "attr", selector: "a.download", payload: "href"}
```

### Execute JavaScript
```
{action: "eval", payload: "document.querySelectorAll('a').length"}
{action: "eval", payload: "Array.from(document.querySelectorAll('a')).map(a => a.href)"}
```

### Resize Viewport (Responsive Testing)
Use `eval` to resize the browser window for testing responsive layouts:
```
{action: "eval", payload: "window.resizeTo(375, 812); 'Resized to mobile'"}
{action: "eval", payload: "window.resizeTo(768, 1024); 'Resized to tablet'"}
{action: "eval", payload: "window.resizeTo(1920, 1080); 'Resized to desktop'"}
```

**Note**: This resizes the window, not device emulation. It won't change:
- Device pixel ratio (retina displays)
- Touch events
- User-Agent string

For most responsive testing, window resize is sufficient.

### Clear Cookies
Use `eval` to clear cookies accessible to JavaScript:
```
{action: "eval", payload: "document.cookie.split(';').forEach(c => { document.cookie = c.trim().split('=')[0] + '=;expires=Thu, 01 Jan 1970 00:00:00 GMT;path=/'; }); 'Cookies cleared'"}
```

**Note**: This clears cookies accessible to JavaScript. It won't clear:
- httpOnly cookies (server-side only)
- Cookies from other domains

For most logout/reset scenarios, this is sufficient.

### Scroll Page
```
{action: "scroll", payload: "down"}
{action: "scroll", payload: "up"}
{action: "scroll", selector: ".container", payload: "{\"deltaX\":0,\"deltaY\":500}"}
```

Uses real mouse wheel events (vs `eval` + `scrollTo` which bot detectors flag).

## Tips

**Always wait before interaction:**
Don't click or fill immediately after navigate - pages need time to load.

```
// BAD - might fail if page slow
{action: "navigate", payload: "https://example.com"}
{action: "click", selector: "button"}  // May fail!

// GOOD - wait first
{action: "navigate", payload: "https://example.com"}
{action: "await_element", selector: "button"}
{action: "click", selector: "button"}
```

**Use specific selectors:**
Avoid generic selectors that match multiple elements.

```
// BAD - matches first button
{action: "click", selector: "button"}

// GOOD - specific
{action: "click", selector: "button[type=submit]"}
{action: "click", selector: "#login-button"}
```

**Submit forms:**
Use `keyboard_press` with Enter after `type`, or append `\n` to the payload.

```
{action: "type", selector: "#search", payload: "query"}
{action: "keyboard_press", payload: "Enter"}
```

**Check content first:**
Extract page content to verify selectors before building workflow.

```
{action: "extract", payload: "html"}
```

## Troubleshooting

**Element not found:**
- Use `await_element` before interaction
- Verify selector with `extract` action using 'html' format

**Timeout errors:**
- Increase timeout: `{timeout: 30000}` for slow pages
- Wait for specific element instead of text

**Wrong tab active:**
- Use `list_tabs` to see all open tabs
- Use `switch_tab` with a URL or title substring to reliably switch tabs
- Tab indices shift when tabs close — prefer URL/title-based switching

**eval returns `[object Object]`:**
- Use `JSON.stringify()` for complex objects: `{action: "eval", payload: "JSON.stringify({name: 'test'})"}`
- For async functions: `{action: "eval", payload: "JSON.stringify(await yourAsyncFunction())"}`

## Test Automation (Advanced)

<details>
<summary>Click to expand test automation guidance</summary>

When building test automation, you have two approaches:

### Approach 1: use_browser MCP (Simple Tests)
Best for: Single-step tests, direct Claude control during conversation

Best for: Multi-step test suites, standalone automation scripts

```bash
./chrome-ws fill 0 "#email" "test@example.com"
./chrome-ws click 0 "button[type=submit]"
./chrome-ws wait-text 0 "Success"
```

1. **Check chrome-ws source code** - It shows the correct CDP pattern
2. **Use chrome-ws to verify** - Test the same operation via CLI
3. **Adapt the pattern** - Apply the working CDP approach to use_browser

- **Form validation**: Fill forms, check error states
- **UI state testing**: Click elements, verify DOM changes
- **Performance testing**: Measure load times, capture metrics
- **Screenshot comparison**: Capture before/after states

</details>

For command-line usage outside Claude Code, see [COMMANDLINE-USAGE.md](COMMANDLINE-USAGE.md).

Full CDP documentation: https://chromedevtools.github.io/devtools-protocol/

Prax ran its own browser measurement and found 3 a11y fails:

1. **a11y.contrast** — 35 failing pairs. Examples:
   - `span` 12px rgb(91,102,114) (#5b6672) on white: ratio measured 2.32?? Wait, #5b6672 on white should be ~5.6:1... Hmm. Let me compute: #5b6672 → relative luminance. R=0x5b=91→0.357 sRGB→lin: ((0.357+0.055)/1.055)^2.4 ≈ (0.390)^2.4 ≈ 0.104. G=0x66=102/255=0.4 → lin ≈ ((0.455)/1.055... let me not compute precisely. Known: #5b6672 vs white — slate-ish 4.5-ish. Measured 2.32? That suggests the checker measured something else — maybe the `.st-idx` spans (12px, ink-3) — but 2.32 doesn't match my math. Actually wait: measured pairs list first_5 includes ratio 1.0 with white on white: `span` 11px bold white-on-white — that's the `.st-mark` (white bg, white text showing "·" or number inside circle)! The mark is a span with color:var(--surface) (#fff) on transparent bg → computed background white → ratio 1. Hmm — the mark span has no background itself (background:var(--surface) — I set `.step-row .st-mark{...border:2px solid...;color:var(--surface);background:var(--surface)}`. I DID set background surface (white). So white text on white bg — the mark shows "·" for pending steps (invisible-ish by design: empty circle) and shows numbers/current in accent. version: "0.1"
screen:
  id: application_shell_screen
  intent:
    primary_task: Walk the single workflow phase-by-phase, satisfying each gate (preconditions, observed-value checks, confirmations) before advancing
    secondary_tasks:
      - Verify observed runtime values against expected values before proceeding past volatile steps
      - Execute contingency branches when a check outcome is not as expected
      - Consult and (where defined) exercise the recovery/rollback path around irreversible steps
      - Review the audit trail of what was done and confirmed
  archetype:
    pattern_ref: PAT-APPLICATION-SHELL
  density_intent: spacious
  regions:
    - id: "Current step: instruction, its gates (checklist / value check / confirmation), and its action"
      role: "experimental:Current step: instruction, its gates (checklist / value check / confirmation), and its action"
      importance: primary
      visibility:
        condition: always
      behavior_intent: []
    - id: "Position and progress: which phase, which step, how far to go (always visible)"
      role: "experimental:Position and progress: which phase, which step, how far to go (always visible)"
      importance: primary
      visibility:
        condition: always
      behavior_intent: []
    - id: "Irreversible-step status: confirmation requirement and recovery path, visible before and after execution"
      role: "experimental:Irreversible-step status: confirmation requirement and recovery path, visible before and after execution"
      importance: primary
      visibility:
        condition: always
      behavior_intent: []
    - id: Audit trail of gates passed, confirmations, verifications, contingencies
      role: experimental:Audit trail of gates passed, confirmations, verifications, contingencies
      importance: supporting
      visibility:
        condition: always
      behavior_intent: []
    - id: Runbook metadata (title, change ref, abort rule)
      role: experimental:Runbook metadata (title, change ref, abort rule)
      importance: supporting
      visibility:
        condition: always
      behavior_intent: []
    - id: Contingency branch outcomes
      role: experimental:Contingency branch outcomes
      importance: supporting
      visibility:
        condition: always
      behavior_intent: []
    - id: workspace
      role: dominant_workspace
      importance: dominant
      visibility:
        condition: always
      behavior_intent:
        - preserve_context
  relationships: []
  interaction_intents:
    - preserve_context
    - keyboard_equivalent
  required_states:
    - loading
    - empty
    - ready
    - selected
    - error
  decision_points:
    - id: region_realization
      question: How should the platform adapter realize the semantic regions while preserving hierarchy?
      adapter_may_choose:
        - native landmarks
        - accessible composite widgets
        - responsive region arrangement
  unresolved: []
  rejected_alternatives:
